Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The method ZipArchiveEntry.isUnixSymlink() intends to determine if a zip entry is a Unix symbolic link. The decision is based on whether the Unix mode has exactly the LINK_FLAG set. The LINK_FLAG is defined as 0120000 (an octal value representing the symlink mode bit in Unix file modes). The method checks if (getUnixMode() & LINK_FLAG) == LINK_FLAG, i.e., all bits of the LINK_FLAG must be set in the Unix mode to identify a symlink.

The getUnixMode() method returns the Unix mode extracted from the external attributes of the entry. It returns 0 if the platform is not Unix (platform != PLATFORM_UNIX). Otherwise, it extracts a 16-bit value from the external attributes shifted and masked accordingly.

The bug report states that for entries with Unix permissions like 177777 (octal), the isUnixSymlink() returns true. Permission 177777 is a weird value where multiple special bits might be set, but the significant part is that the check is only verifying if all bits of the LINK_FLAG are set. However, the intention is that if any other flag bits are set alongside the LINK_FLAG (more than one flag set), then it should not be considered a symlink.

The test checks that when the repository contains an entry "META-INF/maven/" with mode including multiple flags (reported as "rwsrwsrwt" which translates to mode bits including sticky bits and setuid), isUnixSymlink() must return false, but currently, it returns true, thus failing the test.

The root cause is that isUnixSymlink() does a bitwise and with LINK_FLAG and compares it equals LINK_FLAG, which is true even if other bits are set in addition. It does not check that only LINK_FLAG is set and no other bits.

Thus the method doesn't properly handle the case when multiple permission flags are set, only verifying the presence of LINK_FLAG, returning true incorrectly.

Fixing could involve verifying if the mode exactly equals LINK_FLAG or checking no conflicting bits are set alongside LINK_FLAG.

Hence, the bug occurs because isUnixSymlink() checking logic only tests if the symlink bits are set in getUnixMode(), rather than verifying that no other permission flags are concurrently set.

Methods implicated for the bug:
- ZipArchiveEntry.isUnixSymlink()
- Possibly ZipArchiveEntry.getUnixMode() (for interpretation correctness)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
